title: Instrument Usage Agreement Clause on Damage, Normal Wear and Repairs — Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program
content:
**Clause on damage and repair.** Under the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program, normal wear is repaired at no charge, the normal wear charge, because maintenance is part of the usage fee. Damage the director attributes to mishandling, judged against the checkout condition report, is charged the minor repair charge for a minor repair or the major repair charge for a major repair, once per repair order. Repairs take the repair shop's turnaround of calendar days, and a loaner instrument is issued meanwhile when the usage type issues a loaner during repair.

## The clause, condition by condition

| Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The repair is for normal wear | maintenance is part of the usage fee | repaired at the normal wear charge, which is no charge |
| The director attributes the damage to mishandling, judged against the checkout condition report, and it is a minor repair | mishandling, minor | the minor repair charge of the usage type |
| The director attributes the damage to mishandling, judged against the checkout condition report, and it is a major repair | mishandling, major | the major repair charge of the usage type |
| A repair order is charged | one charge per repair order | the charge posts once for that repair order |

**While the instrument is at the shop.** An instrument sent to the district's contracted repair shop is in repair; when the repaired instrument is returned to the student the checkout is again checked out. The repair takes the usage type's turnaround of calendar days. Where the usage type issues a loaner during repair, the student receives a loaner instrument for that time.

**Who attributes the damage.** The director attributes damage to mishandling, and the comparison is with the condition report the director recorded at checkout.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A French horn graded excellent at checkout returns with a dented bell. The director attributes the dent to mishandling by comparison with the excellent grade; a dent is a major repair, so the major repair charge of the usage type is charged once for that repair order.
2. Pads on a woodwind instrument have worn through ordinary use over the year. That is normal wear, and the repair is made at no charge.
3. A violin needs a new bridge after it was dropped, and the director attributes the damage to mishandling. A bridge replacement is a minor repair, charged the minor repair charge once for that repair order.
4. Two separate repair orders are opened on one checkout for two separate mishandling incidents. Each repair order carries its own charge, once.
